title: Project 03 · Milestone 2 — ports and adapters
statement:
Python Engineer · Project

Milestone 2 — ports and adapters

- LinkRepository and ClickRepository Protocols, declared beside the services.

- Two implementations of each: in-memory (tests) and SQLite/Postgres via SQLAlchemy 2.0

async (production).

- Alembic migrations, with an upgrade/downgrade round-trip test.

- UnitOfWork as an async context manager: commit on success, roll back on exception.

- The same service test suite runs against both implementations, via a parametrised

fixture (module 09). If it passes in memory but fails on SQLite, your Protocol is lying.

Build in small increments

  1. List the public interfaces and invariants required by this milestone.
  2. Implement one behavior and write a small test in a test_learner.py file.
  3. Run your tests, then run the required milestone checks.
  4. Record a tradeoff and failure case in Notes before moving on.
Hint

Keep dependencies injectable. Prefer in-memory stores, fake clocks, and scripted clients so behavior is reproducible offline. Use the traceback to find the first missing behavior.

Complete project specification

Project 03 — pulse: a production-grade FastAPI service

Not a tutorial CRUD app. A service you could hand to an on-call rotation: layered,

typed, migrated, authenticated, rate-limited, templated, instrumented, and deployable.

The domain: a link shortener with analytics. Small enough to finish, real enough to

have every hard problem — uniqueness under concurrency, hot-path caching, time-series

aggregation, abuse prevention, and a public redirect endpoint that must never be slow.

Modules it draws on: 05 (errors), 07 (typing), 09 (testing), 11 (async), 14

(architecture), 15 (FastAPI), 16 (Jinja2), 17 (observability).

Milestone 1 — the domain, with no framework in sight

src/pulse/domain/ must not import FastAPI, SQLAlchemy, or anything I/O.

- ShortLink (frozen dataclass): code, target: Url, owner_id, created_at,

expires_at, is_active.

- Value objects: Url (validates scheme and host, rejects javascript: and private

IP ranges — this is an SSRF guard, not decoration), ShortCode (6–12 chars,

base58 alphabet, no 0/O/l/I).

- generate_code(rng) — deterministic under an injected RNG, so tests aren't flaky.

- Domain errors: PulseError base, LinkNotFound, LinkExpired, CodeTaken,

QuotaExceeded.

- 100% unit-tested with no fixtures, no database, no client.

Milestone 2 — ports and adapters

- LinkRepository and ClickRepository Protocols, declared beside the services.

- Two implementations of each: in-memory (tests) and SQLite/Postgres via SQLAlchemy 2.0

async (production).

- Alembic migrations, with an upgrade/downgrade round-trip test.

- UnitOfWork as an async context manager: commit on success, roll back on exception.

- The same service test suite runs against both implementations, via a parametrised

fixture (module 09). If it passes in memory but fails on SQLite, your Protocol is lying.

Milestone 3 — services

- ShortenerService.create(target, owner, custom_code=None, ttl=None) — retries on

CodeTaken up to N times with a fresh random code, honours a per-owner quota, and

emits a LinkCreated event.

- .resolve(code) — returns the target or raises LinkNotFound/LinkExpired, and

records a click without blocking the redirect (a background task / queue).

- AnalyticsService.stats(code, window) — clicks bucketed by hour, plus unique

referrers and top countries.

- Every service takes its dependencies (repos, clock, RNG, bus) as constructor

arguments. Not one module-level singleton.

Milestone 4 — the HTTP layer

MethodPathNotes
POST/api/links201, body validated by pydantic, Location header
GET/api/links/{code}200 / 404
GET/api/linkscursor pagination, not offset
DELETE/api/links/{code}204, owner-only
GET/api/links/{code}/stats200, query-param window
GET/{code}307 redirect, the hot path
GET/health /readyliveness vs readiness — they are different

- Domain exceptions mapped to status codes with @app.exception_handler. No handler

raises HTTPException for a domain condition.

- Auth: API key in a header, resolved to an owner by a dependency; 401 vs 403 used

correctly.

- Per-owner rate limiting with the token bucket you wrote in module 09.

- Cursor pagination (opaque, base64-encoded), because offset pagination breaks under

concurrent inserts.

- ETag + Cache-Control on the redirect, and a small in-process LRU in front of the

repository for hot codes.

Milestone 5 — the HTML side (module 16)

- Jinja2 templates with inheritance: a landing page, a create form, and a stats

dashboard with a chart rendered as inline SVG (no JS build step).

- StrictUndefined, autoescaping on, macros for form fields and flash messages.

- A CSRF token on the form, verified server-side.

- The same handler serves JSON or HTML by Accept header — content negotiation, one

service call, two renderers.

Milestone 6 — operations (module 17)

- OTel tracing on every request and DB call, with service.name and version from

importlib.metadata.

- RED metrics per route, plus domain counters (links.created, links.resolved,

links.expired).

- Structured JSON logs with the trace id, and API keys redacted at the formatter.

- Settings via pydantic-settings, validated at startup: a missing DSN must kill the

process at boot, never at 3am.

- Graceful shutdown: drain in-flight requests, close the pool in the lifespan handler.

- A Dockerfile (multi-stage, non-root, < 200 MB) and a docker-compose.yml with Postgres.

- CI: ruff, mypy --strict, pytest with coverage, and a build.

Going further

- Load-test the redirect with locust or k6; find and fix the first bottleneck.

- Replace the in-process cache with Redis and measure the difference honestly.

- Idempotency keys on POST, so a retried create doesn't make two links.

- OpenAPI schema pinned in CI to catch breaking changes.

- Blue/green migration of a column with zero downtime — write the runbook.

What "done" means

docker compose up, then a fresh clone can create a link, follow the redirect, and see

the click in the dashboard — and mypy --strict and the acceptance suite are both green.

No complete worked solution is provided. Passing checks verifies this milestone’s executable contract; deployment and optional extensions are ungraded.

App check interfaces & required scenarios

These tests define the concrete interfaces used in this app. Read them before choosing file names and method signatures.

test_acceptance.py

"""Acceptance tests for pulse, milestone 1 (the domain).

Run: pytest projects/03_pulse_api -o addopts=""

Note what these tests DON'T need: no database, no client, no fixtures, no async. That is
the payoff of a domain layer that imports nothing.

Milestones 2-6 get their own suites — write them as you go, and make the service tests
parametrised over both repository implementations.
"""

import random
import sys
from datetime import UTC, datetime, timedelta
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).parent / "src"))

domain = pytest.importorskip("pulse.domain")
Url, ShortCode, ShortLink = domain.Url, domain.ShortCode, domain.ShortLink

NOW = datetime(2026, 1, 1, tzinfo=UTC)


class TestUrl:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "raw",
        [
            "https://example.com",
            "http://example.com/path?q=1",
            "https://sub.example.co.uk/a/b#frag",
        ],
    )
    def test_accepts_valid_urls(self, raw):
        assert Url(raw).value

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "raw",
        [
            "javascript:alert(1)",
            "data:text/html,<script>",
            "file:///etc/passwd",
            "ftp://example.com",
            "not a url",
            "",
            "https://",
        ],
    )
    def test_rejects_dangerous_or_malformed(self, raw):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            Url(raw)

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "raw",
        [
            "http://localhost/admin",
            "http://127.0.0.1:8080/",
            "http://10.0.0.5/",
            "http://192.168.1.1/",
            "http://172.16.0.1/",
            "http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/",  # the cloud metadata endpoint
        ],
    )
    def test_rejects_private_addresses(self, raw):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            Url(raw)

    def test_normalises_scheme_and_host(self):
        assert Url("HTTPS://Example.COM/Path").value == "https://example.com/Path"

    def test_strips_default_port(self):
        assert Url("https://example.com:443/x").value == "https://example.com/x"

    def test_length_limit(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            Url("https://example.com/" + "a" * 2100)

    def test_is_frozen_and_hashable(self):
        url = Url("https://example.com")
        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            url.value = "other"
        assert len({Url("https://example.com"), Url("https://example.com")}) == 1


class TestShortCode:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize("raw", ["abc123", "aB3xY9z", "a" * 12])
    def test_accepts_valid(self, raw):
        assert str(ShortCode(raw)) == raw

    @pytest.mark.parametrize(
        "raw", ["abc", "a" * 13, "abc-12", "abc 12", "", "abc0de", "abcOde", "abclde", "abcIde"]
    )
    def test_rejects_invalid(self, raw):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            ShortCode(raw)

    def test_excludes_ambiguous_characters(self):
        # 0/O and l/I are the reason support tickets say "it didn't work".
        for ambiguous in "0OlI":
            with pytest.raises(ValueError):
                ShortCode("abcde" + ambiguous)


class TestGenerateCode:
    def test_length_and_alphabet(self):
        code = domain.generate_code(random.Random(1), length=7)
        assert len(str(code)) == 7
        assert all(c in domain.BASE58 for c in str(code))

    def test_is_deterministic_under_a_seed(self):
        a = domain.generate_code(random.Random(42))
        b = domain.generate_code(random.Random(42))
        assert str(a) == str(b)

    def test_different_seeds_differ(self):
        a = domain.generate_code(random.Random(1))
        b = domain.generate_code(random.Random(2))
        assert str(a) != str(b)

    def test_collisions_are_rare(self):
        rng = random.Random(0)
        codes = {str(domain.generate_code(rng)) for _ in range(5000)}
        assert len(codes) == 5000


class TestShortLink:
    def link(self, **overrides):
        defaults = {
            "code": ShortCode("abc123"),
            "target": Url("https://example.com"),
            "owner_id": "owner-1",
            "created_at": NOW,
        }
        return ShortLink(**{**defaults, **overrides})

    def test_defaults(self):
        link = self.link()
        assert link.is_active is True
        assert link.expires_at is None

    def test_never_expires_without_expires_at(self):
        assert self.link().is_expired(NOW + timedelta(days=3650)) is False

    def test_expiry(self):
        link = self.link(expires_at=NOW + timedelta(hours=1))
        assert link.is_expired(NOW) is False
        assert link.is_expired(NOW + timedelta(hours=2)) is True

    def test_naive_datetime_rejected(self):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError):
            self.link(expires_at=NOW + timedelta(hours=1)).is_expired(datetime(2026, 1, 2))

    def test_deactivate_returns_a_new_link(self):
        link = self.link()
        deactivated = link.deactivate()
        assert deactivated.is_active is False
        assert link.is_active is True
        assert deactivated is not link

    def test_frozen(self):
        with pytest.raises(Exception):
            self.link().owner_id = "someone-else"


class TestErrors:
    def test_hierarchy(self):
        for cls in (domain.LinkNotFound, domain.LinkExpired, domain.CodeTaken, domain.QuotaExceeded):
            assert issubclass(cls, domain.PulseError)

    def test_messages_and_payloads(self):
        assert str(domain.LinkNotFound("abc123")) == "link 'abc123' not found"
        assert domain.CodeTaken("abc123").code == "abc123"
        assert domain.QuotaExceeded("owner-1", 100).limit == 100


class TestLayering:
    def test_domain_imports_no_frameworks(self):
        """The architectural rule, as an executable test."""
        source = (Path(__file__).parent / "src/pulse/domain/__init__.py").read_text()
        for banned in ("fastapi", "sqlalchemy", "pydantic", "httpx", "redis"):
            assert banned not in source.lower(), f"domain must not import {banned}"

test_milestones.py

import asyncio
import pytest


class TestMilestone2:
    @pytest.mark.parametrize('backend',['memory','sqlite'])
    def test_repository_roundtrip_duplicate_and_transaction(self,backend,tmp_path):
        from pulse.repositories import MemoryLinkRepository,SQLiteLinkRepository
        from pulse.domain import ShortLink,ShortCode,Url,CodeTaken
        from datetime import datetime,timezone
        async def scenario():
            repo=MemoryLinkRepository() if backend=='memory' else SQLiteLinkRepository(tmp_path/'links.db')
            link=ShortLink(code=ShortCode('abc123'),target=Url('https://example.com'),owner_id='owner',created_at=datetime(2026,1,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc))
            await repo.add(link)
            assert (await repo.get('abc123')).target==link.target
            with pytest.raises(CodeTaken):await repo.add(link)
            with pytest.raises(RuntimeError):
                async with repo.transaction():
                    await repo.delete('abc123')
                    raise RuntimeError('rollback')
            assert await repo.get('abc123') is not None
            if backend=='sqlite':
                reopened=SQLiteLinkRepository(tmp_path/'links.db')
                assert (await reopened.get('abc123')).target==link.target
        asyncio.run(scenario())


class TestMilestone3:
    def test_services_create_resolve_and_enforce_quota(self):
        from pulse.services import ShortenerService
        from pulse.repositories import MemoryLinkRepository,MemoryClickRepository
        from pulse.domain import QuotaExceeded,LinkNotFound
        from datetime import datetime,timezone
        import random
        async def scenario():
            links,clicks=MemoryLinkRepository(),MemoryClickRepository();events=[]
            service=ShortenerService(links=links,clicks=clicks,clock=lambda:datetime(2026,1,1,tzinfo=timezone.utc),rng=random.Random(7),bus=events.append,quota=1)
            link=await service.create('https://example.com','owner')
            assert str(await service.resolve(str(link.code)))=='https://example.com'
            with pytest.raises(QuotaExceeded):await service.create('https://other.example','owner')
            with pytest.raises(LinkNotFound):await service.resolve('zzzzzz')
            assert len(events)==1
        asyncio.run(scenario())


class TestMilestone4:
    def test_http_contract(self):
        from pulse.app import create_app
        from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
        client=TestClient(create_app(testing=True))
        assert client.get('/health').status_code==200
        assert client.post('/api/links',json={'target':'https://example.com'}).status_code==401
        headers={'X-API-Key':'course-test-key'}
        response=client.post('/api/links',json={'target':'https://example.com'},headers=headers)
        assert response.status_code==201 and response.headers['location']
        code=response.json()['code']
        redirect=client.get('/'+code,follow_redirects=False)
        assert redirect.status_code==307 and redirect.headers['location']=='https://example.com'
        assert redirect.headers['etag'] and redirect.headers['cache-control']
        assert client.get('/api/links',headers=headers).status_code==200
        assert client.delete('/api/links/'+code,headers=headers).status_code==204


class TestMilestone5:
    def test_html_escape_content_negotiation_and_csrf(self):
        from pulse.app import create_app
        from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
        client=TestClient(create_app(testing=True))
        page=client.get('/',headers={'Accept':'text/html'})
        assert page.status_code==200 and 'text/html' in page.headers['content-type']
        assert 'csrf' in page.text.lower()
        assert client.post('/links',data={'target':'https://example.com'}).status_code==403
        from pulse.templates import environment
        env=environment()
        assert env.from_string('{{ value }}').render(value='<script>')=='<script>'
        with pytest.raises(Exception): env.from_string('{{ missing }}').render()


class TestMilestone6:
    def test_settings_and_safe_logs(self):
        from pulse.operations import Settings,format_log
        with pytest.raises(ValueError): Settings(dsn='')
        log=format_log({'message':'request','api_key':'secret','trace_id':'abc'})
        assert 'secret' not in log and 'abc' in log

    def test_lifespan_closes_owned_resources(self):
        from pulse.app import create_app
        from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
        app=create_app(testing=True)
        with TestClient(app) as client:
            assert client.get('/ready').status_code==200
            pool=app.state.pool
        assert pool.closed is True

"""pulse — a link shortener with analytics, built like a service you have to operate.

Layering rule, enforced by review and by your own discipline:

    api/       FastAPI routers, pydantic schemas, templates   -> imports services
    services/  use cases, transactions, events                -> imports domain
    domain/    entities, value objects, errors                -> imports NOTHING
    adapters/  repositories, cache, clock                     -> implements the Protocols

`domain/` importing FastAPI or SQLAlchemy is the moment the architecture died.
"""
